cm848_field_renames.evidence: CM848's own e2m (CHR_CC_11.45.01.07) names this bit: 106B +8 ANC_Fuel_Algorithm_Enable [NZFLAGEN], S mask 0x1000, 'Enable for fuel limiting of the acceleration noise control algorithm'. The CM848 struct comment already cites it, but the field stayed reserved because there is no reader (the ANC stage is compiled out). Other no-reader CM848 bits are named from their e2m records (idle_speed_adjust_enable, j1922_monitor_enable, the fan bits). CM550 tests the same mask at 0xb2c6 (cm550_rpm_system_state_controller computes _anc_fuel_limit_value).

CM848's own e2m: 106B +8 ANC_Timing_Algorithm_Enable [NZTAAGEN], S mask 0x2000, 'Enable for timing advance of the acceleration noise control algorithm'. There is no CM848 reader. CM550 tests 0x2000 at 0xb3ec (cm550_FUN_0000b3d0, the ANC timing limit: _anc_timing_limit_disable_due_to_bare_engine_accel).

CM848's own e2m: 106B +8 ANC_Speed_Algorithm_Enable [NZESAGEN], S mask 0x4000, 'Enable for speed limiting of the acceleration noise control algorithm'. There is no CM848 reader. CM550 tests 0x4000 at 0xb50e (cm550_engineStateFuelLimitInterpolator, the ANC engine speed limit).

Reviewer's call: the current name is a code-derived description, not a reserved bit. CM848's own e2m has no record for 0x100. CM848's own code only acts on this bit outside the top gear range: cm848_calculateRoadSpeedGovernorFueling and cm848_selectCruiseGovernorGainSet test it together with drivetrain_gear_range != DRIVETRAIN_GEAR_RANGE_TOP_GEAR. CM848's drivetrain_gear_range row already calls it 'the gear-down feature (algorithm_enable_flags_3_cal bit 0x100)'. The same Cummins table names the bit in CM550's e2m (GRGDPNEN 'GEAR DOWN PROTECTION ENABLE, BIT 8 OF 0-15') and in another Chrysler e2m (CHR_B2_11.52.08.72 Gear_Down_Protection_Enable, S mask 0x100). CM550 has no reader for it in the dumped ROM.

proposal.notes: Method: hits.py (scratch) scanned J90350.00.rom.bin for every absolute-long reference to 0x803c92-0x803ca1 and decoded each instruction. All 75 references are word reads: either move.w abs,Dn followed by andi.w/andi.l with a single-bit mask, or movea.l #0x803c94,A0 followed by move.w (0,A0,Dn.w*2). There is no store, no btst, no byte access, no access to any odd address, and no access to 0x803c92. A search of the 16-bit low halves found no other access form. The only other references are generic EEPROM-mirror code (cm550_commitEepromMirrorToEeprom, the memory read handlers, cm550_memoryPatchingSystem). Every mask tested is a single bit, so the bitfield types render without multi-bit pieces. I cite each test by its instruction address and mask. hits.py names the nearest preceding function start, and several hosts overlap or are misnamed: 0x1ca54/0x1ca5c, 0x26474/0x26484, 0x30a5e/0x30a64. The word 3 bit 1 test at 0x33d80 lies in an undefined function at 0x33d38, which sends j1939_pgn65252_tx_message (PGN 65252 SHUTDN) via cm550_sendCanMessage. Word 0 check: the claim holds. The indexed tests use word 0 (0x803c94) as their base and reach words 7+ (protection channels: bits 0x70-0x72 + 4n), 13+ (switches: 0xd0 + n) and 26+ (0x1a0 + n), never words 0-6. Word 0 therefore stays a plain word, like CM848's (the fault-word rule: a struct base would print as field_0x0 pieces). Its bit meanings are in the row comment, and its fields list is for that comment only. Word 6 is a plain word by judgment: its only reader is the whole-word load at 0xbccc, so a bitfield would give no named test and would turn that load into a piece. The alternative, cm550_algorithm_enable_flags_6_t, would take the listed fields unchanged. Word 5 is a bitfield trade-off: 7 named single-bit tests (0x400 six times, 0x800 once) against 1 piece (the whole-word load at 0xb7d2). Word 5 field names follow the channel record names (bit n = channel n; the loop restarts its mask at channel 16 on word 6), so bit 9 is exhaust_pressure even though v64t6_s's text says SPARE_CHANNEL_1. Pilot correction: pilot_bitfield_r92.py placed j1922_monitor_clear_enable at bit 1, following JC22CCSW's text 'BIT 1'. The code tests 0x100 for it at 0x1fd6c (the J1922 clear occurrence time), and CM848's S mask is 0x100, so it is bit 8 and bit 1 is reserved. The pilot's bit 6 name engine_brake_enable should be CM848's engine_retarder_clutch_deactivation_enable. Several N records in v64t6_s give no bit in their text (LSAGGNEN, LSHGGNEN, LSMGGNEN, LSJCGNEN, JC22MRSW, JC39MREA, JCRDTXEA, NZESAGEN, NZFLAGEN, NZTAAGEN). Each is placed by CM848's S mask, and the CM550 code tests the same mask. Text that v64t6_s truncates (PTRXEN 'REMOTE PTO IS ALLO(WED)', ISRPEN, ISIMEN, CPAGEN) and some S masks (PTRXEN 0x20, Gear_Down_Protection_Enable 0x100, Fuel_Log_Enable 0x200) come from other e2m files in e2m-analysis. 'No reader' always means no reader in the dumped ROM (0x0-0x3FFFF). Calls go to undumped targets at 0x40000+, and word 3 = 0x86e8 has cruise, road speed governor, remote PTO, droop and save-set-speed set with no reader. Dump values (EEPROM = RAM): length 0x0046; words 0-6 = 0x5c10, 0x1000, 0x1870, 0x86e8, 0x0000, 0x0000, 0x0000. The length row uses word: -1. shared_with_cm848 = true means the row takes CM848's bitfield type, as words 1 and 4 do; plain words are false. Each row comment ends with a (was ...) note where a row exists; words 4 and 6 and the length word have no row now. Asides (no rename proposed, outside this batch): vp44_communication_state_machine 0x13616 is the data collector sampler; vp44SensorStatusMonitor 0x1d9b4 is the idle shutdown state machine; cm550_oil_pressure_shutdown_controller 0x2dcb0 is the PTO / user fueling selection (CM848 twin cm848_selectPowerTakeOffOrUserFueling); insiteCommandByteDispatcher parameter 0x47 is J1587 PID 71, the idle shutdown timer status; the cm550_eps* functions at 0x2609c-0x265e6 are the low speed governor gain-set logic. The scratch scripts are /home/linux/.claude/jobs/374b0424/tmp/w15/r92/scratch/W1/hits.py and longest_desc.py (with longest_desc.txt).

verdict.overall: Re-checked from scratch. Method: scanned the ROM for every 32-bit value 0x803c92-0x803ca1 at any alignment (plus the EEPROM form 0x01000188-0x010001cf and the 16-bit low halves), wrote a small CPU32 disassembler (llvm-mc's m68k decoder rejects andi / tst and resynchronises silently) and read every site, read both dumps as words, pulled CM848's raw S masks, compared the CM848 twins, and matched each word 5 / 6 bit to its channel's own block 1003 records in v64t6_s. Result: no name, type or bit position moves - 118 CONFIRMED, 6 AMENDED, 0 REFUTED. All six amendments are comment or differences-text fixes: (1) length word: the region list entry is at 0x80ea, not 0x80e8; (2) word 2: the differences text says CM848 reads bit 7 - it does not (no reader for bits 7 and 8 there); (3) and (4) word 2 bits 7 and 11: the tests are andi.w (0240 0080 / 0240 0800), not andi.l; (5) and (6) word 6 row comment and bit 9: ISIMEN's '0 = the ambient air temperature' reading is a guess (the text is cut at '0 - AMBIENT TEMP = DO' in every e2m and the bit has no reader). For the orchestrator, from inside CONFIRMED rows: the ROM has 74 references to these words, not the 75 in the notes (23 + 11 + 16 + 13 + 2 + 8 + 1; the proposer's own hits.py prints 74), and two of them (0xb7d2, 0xbccc) are whole-word loads to d5, not single-bit tests; every other one is a word read followed by andi with one bit, or one of the 15 indexed base loads (bit numbers from 112 / 0xd0 / 0x1a0 up, never words 0-6); no store, no btst, no byte access, no based (d16,An) access. The shared claims for words 1 and 4 hold bit for bit. The word 5 bit 9 comment should cite CM550's own ADSYEPCA 'ENGINE_SYNC_EXHAUST_PRESSURE_CHANNEL_ADDRESS' rather than the other product's ADEXPROD. The four CM848 renames are supported (12-14 by CM848's own e2m S masks; 8 is optional convergence - the current name is not wrong); if bit 8 is renamed, update the algorithm_enable_flags_3_cal row comment ('bit 8 has no record (the road speed governor without droops below top gear)') and the CM550 word 3 bit 8 field comment. Scratch (read-only tools and the verdict file): /home/linux/.claude/jobs/374b0424/tmp/w15/r92/scratch/W1/skeptic/ (m68k.py, site.py, based.py, channels.py, all_e2m_106b.py, build_verdicts.py, verdicts_W1.json).

One address in the comment is wrong: the region list is 8-byte [address][length] pairs from 0x8082 (0x80e2 = 0x00060000 / 0x9e, 0x80ea = 0x01000188 / 0x48), so the entry is at 0x80ea, not 0x80e8.

verdicts.reason: 0x803c94 = 106B +2 (EEPROM 0x18a). My own census gives 23 references: 8 move.w (0x803c94).l,d0 + andi with one bit (0xc3ba 0x4000; 0xc5a0 0x400; 0xc5b4 0x800; 0xc5cc 0x1000; 0xc5e4 0x2000; 0xc5fc 0x8000; 0x13630 0x100; 0x1ca86 andi.l 0x40) and 15 movea.l #0x803c94,a0 + move.w (0,a0,dn.w*2). I disassembled all 15: the bit numbers start at 112 / 113 / 114 (+4 per channel; +2 / +3 in cm550_diagnosticProtectionEvaluator and cm550_protectionState1DiagnosticValidator), 0x1a0 (+1 per channel) and 0xd0 + switch, so they reach words 7+, 13+ and 26+ only. No store, no byte or btst access. 0x5c10 in both dumps. CM848's word 0 is a plain word for the same reason and has the extra S record 0x2 (AFC_Low_Boost_Derate_Enable, which its code reads); CM550's e2m has 12 N records, bits 4-15. A plain word with the bits in the comment is right.
No record for mask 0x1 at 106B +2 in v64t6_s, no test of that mask on 0x803c94, clear in 0x5c10 (comment only: word 0 stays a word).
No CM550 record for 0x2 and no test of it; CM848's e2m has AFC_Low_Boost_Derate_Enable S 0x2 and its code tests '& 2'; clear in 0x5c10 (comment only).
No record for mask 0x4 at 106B +2 in v64t6_s, no test of that mask on 0x803c94, clear in 0x5c10 (comment only: word 0 stays a word).
No record for mask 0x8 at 106B +2 in v64t6_s, no test of that mask on 0x803c94, clear in 0x5c10 (comment only: word 0 stays a word).

EBODEN N 'BIT 6 OF 0-15 ... ENABLES FSO VAL(VE TO CLOSE ON'; S 0x40 elsewhere). 0x1ca86 move.w, 0x1ca8c andi.l #0x40: reached only with 0x80a9c8 (engine_retarder_active_flag) non-zero, and a set bit takes the branch that clears bit 0x20 of fuel_system_output_driver_control. Clear in the dumps.

0x803c9e = 106B +C (EEPROM 0x194). 8 references: the whole-word load to d5 at 0xb7d2 and 7 single-bit reads (0x400 at 0x10584, 0x1083e, 0x20cae, 0x20e4a, 0x2582e, 0x32f78; 0x800 at 0x32fd8); no store; 0x0000 in the dumps. So bit n = channel n. In CM550's own e2m the OD record with mask 1 << n has the stem of channel n's block 1003 record for all 16 (checked from the CA / HE / LE records). The word is tested and never written, so a bitfield suits it (7 named tests against one whole-word load). CM848's word 5 is a different set, so the type is CM550's own.
